answer: Capital loans price sybils out: every identity funds its trades against locked collateral from a liquidity pool, and loans to young identities carry punitive interest, like cracking a walnut with bare hands - possible once, ruinous a thousand times. A shell of fakes with no history pays a hollow premium on every loan, while one honest identity earns an opal-clear rate by aging. A farmer's thousand fakes each borrow separately, so interest compounds across the fleet, while the honest agent's loan costs almost nothing. Cloning keys multiplies the interest bill, not the buying power.
